These tournaments are categorized by the Average Quality (AVQ) range of the teams that can participate. Here's how the system creates them:  The system checks to see which tournament categories are currently active. It determines whether at least one tournament already exists in each of the following categories:  Low AVQ Medium AVQ High AVQ All AVQ  New Tournament Creation: If a tournament category does not have any active tournaments, the system creates a new tournament for that category.  Tournament Categories: The four categories created and the criteria to join are the following:  Low AVQ: AVQ Range: Teams with an AVQ between 0 and 52 (randomly generated between 50 and 52). Entry Fee: 5 Teams Limit: 16  Medium AVQ: AVQ Range: Teams with an AVQ between 0 and 57 (randomly generated between 53 and 57). Entry Fee: 5 Teams Limit: 16  High AVQ: AVQ Range: Teams with an AVQ between 0 and 68 (randomly generated between 58 and 68). Entry Fee: 10 Teams Limit: 10  All AVQ: AVQ Range: Teams with an AVQ between 52 and 100. Entry Fee: 10 Teams Limit: 10  Tournament Settings: All the newly created tournaments will have the following rules set Start Date : Will start in 24 hours (auto-start) Teams needed to start : 8 for low and medium tournaments, 6 for high and all tournaments

[2025-01-30 17:48] maridiba : League Prize is computed the same way in every nation, and it's completely funded from the Federation fund of that nation; that fund collects money from all the clubs of the nation when they pay for salaries, youth pulls, staff, taxes on CC/CL prizes and stadium tickets...  So, if in nation 1 the prize is higher than in nation 2, it means that in the previous season, the teams in nation 1 have sent more money to their National Fund. That's not a secret, the funds and their transactions are visible, just check it and you will figure out where the prizes come from

[2025-04-05 19:10] maridiba : Do you guys know the infamous roulette Martingale scam? The one where you should play red/black and always double the bet when you lose, to always make a profit
[2025-04-05 19:11] maridiba : In theory it's not a scam, it always works, provided you have funds to double the previous bet
[2025-04-05 19:12] maridiba : After all, how many times can you get the same color in a row?
[2025-04-05 19:15] maridiba : In practice, it is a scam because extreme events exist... no matters how much budget you have, if you keep trying you will eventually get a series long enough to drain all your funds, even if you start betting 1 cent and you have 1 million budget (which would be not appealing anyway)
[2025-04-05 19:17] maridiba : When probability is involved, the system doesn't have to "try" to simulate surprise results. They will automatically happen once in a while, it's unavoidable

[2025-05-25 12:56] nicmo7829 : I totally get your frustration — it's clear you've put a lot of time and thought into how you play, and when the game mechanics seem to fight you rather than reward smart tactics, it can be incredibly disheartening. But I wanted to offer a bit of a different perspective, or at least try to unpack some of what might be going on.  First off, the yellow/red card issue with hard tackling — you're right, it’s harsh in the current state of the game. The frequency of bookings, especially double yellows within such a short time span, can feel more like a dice roll than a reflection of tactical nuance. That said, I don’t think the intent is to make hard tackle "unusable," but rather to make it something you deploy with caution and in specific situations — not a blanket setting you can use for entire matches like in older games. Is that perfect balance achieved yet? Honestly, probably not. But I suspect part of the challenge is that KoB is trying to be a bit more dynamic and reactive than some of the older football manager games that were easier to “solve” with one aggressive setup.  What’s different here is that squad management is part of the tactical layer. I actually find it interesting that KoB kind of forces you to think beyond your best XI. Having to maintain a bigger squad, rotate due to cards, injuries, or fatigue — yeah, it’s punishing, but it also mirrors the chaos and unpredictability of real-world football. You can’t go all out every game without consequences. I do agree though that fatigue and injuries might be a little too frequent, especially when combined with the card system. It pushes the balance toward frustration more than realism sometimes.
[2025-05-25 12:56] nicmo7829 : As for losing games to penalties even with solid defenders — man, that stings. But I’ve seen that too, and in my experience, it’s not always just about having high XP or tackling attributes. Positioning, decision-making, and yes, even luck, seem to play a big role. I’ve noticed veteran defenders sometimes commit more errors simply because they’re slower or more aggressive than young, balanced ones. That said, if seasoned defenders are consistently underperforming, that might be worth reporting — could be an area the devs need to tweak.  The biggest takeaway I’d offer is this: KoB rewards adaptation, but it’s still maturing. You can win without going fully aggressive or keeping a 30-man squad — but you’ll need to find a tactical sweet spot that minimizes risk while still being competitive. And yeah, that can be tough with the current match engine quirks. But that’s why feedback like yours matters. Rants are fine (I’ve had my share of them too), but maybe try channeling that into specific examples for the devs — game minutes, player stats, tackle types, etc. The more data they have, the better chance they’ll balance things in future updates.  TL;DR — you're not wrong to be annoyed, and the current system might need tuning. But don't give up just yet — experiment a bit, mix defensive lines, consider morale effects, and most of all, keep pressing for improvements. It’s a work in progress, and your voice (especially with how passionate you clearly are) can help shape it.

[2025-10-01 10:22] nicmo7829 : anyway, i have been thinking of a solution to further balance local rewards (yes a lot was done in the past) and it would be something similar to how division wages weight works.  We would calculate the percentage each team pays in wages in that specific league, so the 16 teams would sum up to 100%, and then match the league prize percentage to each position. For example: if the most expensive (in wages) team spends 30% of the total wages from that series, the prize for 1st in that series would be 30% of the allocated funds for that series. The 2nd position would also get the % of the total prize as the % of the 2nd team that pays the most wages, and so on for the 16 positions.  This would mean your wages would serve as your season expectations, if the club finishes above your wages position, you make a profit as you did better than expected for the wages you pay, if you finish below you lose money.

[2026-02-26 19:33] nicmo7829 : At its simplest, flooding is an overflow of water that submerges land that is usually dry. While it’s a natural part of the Earth's water cycle, it can also be triggered or worsened by human activity and infrastructure failure.  Floods aren't just "too much rain"; they are complex events categorized by how they start and where the water goes. Common Types of Flooding      Fluvial (River Floods): Occurs when a river's water level rises above its banks, often due to excessive rain or rapid snowmelt upstream.      Pluvial (Surface Floods): Happens when heavy rainfall creates a flood independent of a body of water. This is common in urban areas where the ground or drainage systems can't absorb the water fast enough.      Coastal Floods: Driven by extreme sea-level rises caused by storms (storm surges), high tides, or tsunamis.      Flash Floods: Characterized by a rapid rise of water (within six hours) in low-lying areas, usually caused by intense thunderstorms or sudden dam breaks. They are particularly dangerous because of their speed and force.  What Causes Floods?  The "why" behind flooding usually falls into three buckets:      Meteorological: Intense or prolonged rainfall, hurricanes, and rapid snowmelt.      Hydrological: Saturated soil that can no longer soak up water, or ice jams in rivers that act as temporary dams.      Human-Made: Urbanization (replacing soil with concrete), deforestation, and the failure of levees or dams.  Why It Matters  Beyond the immediate physical damage, flooding reshapes the landscape by depositing nutrient-rich silt (good for farming) but also carries pollutants and disrupts ecosystems. From a human perspective, it remains one of the most frequent and costly natural disasters globally.      Note: Just a few inches of fast-moving water can knock an adult off their feet or sweep away a vehicle.
